episodes.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
episodes.about: My guest today is Hayden Field, The Verge's senior AI reporter, and we're discussing the Anthropic IPO for our third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. So you'll hear Hayden and I dive into this tension, and what to make of Anthropic's unique corporate governance structure in the wake of the Jensen Huang saga.
episodes.why: Hayden Field, The Verge's senior AI reporter, walks through the tension at the center of Anthropic's public debut: whether a company beholden to shareholders can keep spending on safety, and what its unusual governance structure actually allows.

episodes.title: Inside China’s new AI propaganda machine: The GoLaxy papers
episodes.about: Leaked documents from a Chinese company reveal an unsettling new kind of information warfare: armies of AI-generated personas designed to look like us, sound like us, and earn our trust. Vanderbilt researchers Brett Goldstein and Brett Benson uncovered the operation. And what they found suggests the future of propaganda is already here.
episodes.why: Leaked GoLaxy documents show a Chinese company building armies of AI-generated personas meant to look and sound like ordinary people and earn their trust; Vanderbilt researchers Brett Goldstein and Brett Benson explain how they uncovered the operation.

episodes.title: Gemini and the path to AGI with Koray Kavukcuoglu
episodes.about: Seven years after their last conversation at Google DeepMind's London office, Professor Hannah Fry reunites with Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP of Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google. Back then, DeepMind was focused on specialized breakthroughs like AlphaGo and AlphaFold; today, Koray is leading the charge toward general-purpose intelligence with Gemini. In this episode, they discuss why real-world products are essential to building AGI, how Gemini's architecture continuously evolves, and the topic on everyone's mind: recursive self-improvement.
episodes.why: DeepMind's chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu tells Hannah Fry why shipping real products is now central to the AGI push, how Gemini's architecture keeps changing under the hood, and where recursive self-improvement fits in the plan.

episodes.title: How an American AI Company Uses Chinese Open-Weight Models
episodes.about: This week, we got news that the Trump administration is reportedly considering a requirement for US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models. Any effort to discourage US businesses from using Chinese open-source could be a big deal for both the AI industry and the market, where investors are still debating whether customers will ultimately be willing to pay for pricier homegrown frontier models versus cheaper alternatives. Everyone remembers last year's 'DeepSeek moment' for AI, when a Chinese company released a cheaper model that seemed nearly as good as cutting-edge US ones. So why do businesses actually use open-source? In this episode, we talk to Daniel Saedi, co-founder of Minerva, to better understand how an AI native company chooses its models. He breaks down how exactly his company mixes and matches models for specific use cases, the risk of abliterated models, and the issue of data sovereignty.
episodes.why: Washington is reportedly considering making US companies disclose their use of Chinese AI models; Minerva co-founder Daniel Saedi explains why his company mixes cheaper open-weight models with frontier ones, and what the risk of an 'abliterated' model looks like in practice.

episodes.title: Why Is Everything Breaking? Plus: Anthropic’s $1.5 Trillion IPO
episodes.about: Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, United, the NSA and Apple all went down within one week. Officials say none of the outages were cyberattacks, but the internet isn't buying it. WIRED's senior business editor Sophie Kleeman joins Brian and Leah to discuss what actually went wrong and why people jumped straight to blaming hackers and AI. They also cover Anthropic's IPO at a reported $1.5 trillion, Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned, and the administration's new rule to stop Chinese companies from renting AI chips just before Trump meets Xi.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Uncanny Valley is WIRED's tech-culture show, new to this list; after Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, United and Apple all went down in one week, WIRED's Sophie Kleeman separates what actually failed from the hacker and AI theories that filled the gap.
